sub_criteria.name: baseline recall ceiling
sub_criteria.text: Reports or measures the recall/precision ceiling of single-query database search (BM25, embedding search, or a search API) as a comparison point.

sub_criteria.name: agentic mechanism gain
sub_criteria.text: Attributes a measured gain to a specific agentic move — query reformulation, citation-graph traversal, or iterative crawling — rather than to the system as an undifferentiated whole.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval/reranking method
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates a retrieval or reranking technique underlying an agentic literature-search system (dense retrieval, learned reranker, hybrid search).

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Explains how an evaluation set for literature-search agents was built — query source, relevance labeling, corpus coverage, contamination controls.

sub_criteria.name: gain replication failure
sub_criteria.text: Shows a reported agentic gain shrinking, disappearing, or failing to generalize under a different benchmark, metric, or independent replication.

items.abstract_600: Current benchmarks for evaluating software engineering agents, such as SWE-Bench Verified, are predominantly derived from GitHub issues and fail to accurately reflect how developers interact with chat-based coding assistants in integrated development environments (IDEs). items.title: What Do Machine Learning Researchers Mean by “Reproducible”?
items.abstract_600: The concern that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are entering a "reproducibility crisis" has spurred significant research in the past few years. Yet with each paper, it is often unclear what someone means by "reproducibility". Our work attempts to clarify the scope of "reproducibility" as displayed by the community at large. In doing so, we propose to refine the research to eight general topic areas. items.abstract_600: Automated Program Repair (APR) agents leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to autonomously diagnose and fix software bugs through reasoning, planning, and tool use. items.abstract_600: The rapid advancement of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has significantly enhanced performance across benchmarks. items.abstract_600: The global burden of mental health challenges, particularly among students and young adults, necessitates innovative digital solutions that are both accessible and effective. items.abstract_600: This work introduces LEGOB ENCH, a benchmark for evaluating systems that generate leaderboards and a collection of leaderboard data curated from PapersWithCode, citation network, and comparison network curated from twenty-two years of arXiv.

items.abstract_600: Despite growing awareness of problems with fairness in artificial intelligence (AI) models in radiology, evaluation of algorithmic biases, or AI biases, remains challenging due to various complexities. items.abstract_600: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools, such as Large Language Models (LLMs), are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains to support decision-making, situational awareness, and knowledge synthesis. items.abstract_600: Recently, the advent of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized generative agents. items.abstract_600: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) plays an important role in many domains such as finance, transportation, and healthcare. items.abstract_600: This study evaluates the efficiency of code generation by Large Language Models (LLMs) and measures their performance against human-crafted solutions using a dataset from Leetcode.
